_about: TRANSLATOR SHELF: John Florio (1553?-1625). Montaigne's Essayes (1603) in the Gibbings 1906 reprint (6 vols, Toronto copies, raw OCR) and the 1620 English Decameron as attributed to him (PG). PD. Added 2026-10-02 at the coordinator's relay; Adam may veto the whole shelf. No uids minted in the relay burst.

florio-decameron-1: Boccaccio, The Decameron, Days 1-5 (1620 tr., attributed to Florio)

florio-decameron.note: Published anonymously in 1620; the attribution to Florio is scholarly (PG credits him). Dryden's three Boccaccio tales are a different translation (dryden-fables-boccaccio).

_pending.florio-montaigne-1603-folio: The 1603 first edition (IA MontaigneImages / McGill 1632 folio): only images or long-s OCR; the 1906 reprint is used.
_pending.florio-montaigne-everyman: Everyman (1910) or Temple Classics (1897) Florio sets: alternate witnesses if the Gibbings OCR proves weak.

_excluded.pg-56200: Queen Anna's New World of Words: Florio's dictionary, not a translation (could join a lexicon shelf, Adam's call).
_excluded.pg-3600-cotton: PG's Montaigne Essays is Charles Cotton's translation, not Florio.
